note: Rewritten from Hagen 1858, a Latin diagnosis followed by a German description (Monographie der Termiten, the key to the species of Hodotermes before no. 43 and the entry for H. ochraceus). Hagen used the combination Hodotermes ochraceus Burmeister, 1839, which is the present Anacanthotermes ochraceus, the type species of Anacanthotermes; the entry is that species. Type locality Egypt. The author examined 11 dried alates of both sexes from different lots and considered them fully coloured and not immature. The original mixes old German orthography (Thier, Fühler and so on) with the page markers of the Google Books scan (p. 85, 86, Digitized by Google); plate I fig. 9, plate II fig. 3 and plate III figs 7 and 42 have not been translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The species are divided into two groups by the wing membrane and the lateral spines of the tibiae: H. ochraceus and H. vagans have an opaque wing membrane and no lateral tibial spines; H. viator and H. mossambicus have a transparent wing membrane and lateral tibial spines. The species differs from H. vagans as follows: the pronotum is narrower than the head but slightly larger than in H. vagans, its anterior margin wider, more strongly projecting forwards and more upturned, the transverse groove extending further into the anterior corners, the anterior corners right-angled and strongly upturned; the wings are longer and wider than in H. vagans, the anterior margin more curved, the subcosta slightly further away and with about 7 oblique branches, of which the second arises at the wing scale and forks twice, and from the middle 3 conspicuous horny branches run towards the media; the media divides into two similar simple branches only in the posterior half of the wing, or splits at the posterior margin; the submedia has about 8 oblique branches; the wing membrane is dull and has irregular fine veins throughout; the whole body is more densely hairy.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Latin diagnosis: body ochraceous, wings opaque, margin and marginal vein yellowish; frons shining; posterior margin of the pronotum rounded; media forked at the apex; outer side of the tibiae without spines. Measurements: length including the wings 24 mm; body length 10 mm; wing span 46 mm. German description: uniformly ochraceous yellow throughout, the head slightly reddish yellow; wings dull, dirty yellowish white, the marginal area slightly more yellow. Head large, almost circular, smooth and shining, the sides less declivous; ocelli indistinct. Antennae 26-segmented, similar to those of H. vagans, tapering towards the apex. Pronotum narrower than the head, slightly larger than in H. vagans; anterior margin wider, more strongly projecting forwards and more upturned; transverse groove extending further into the anterior corners; anterior corners right-angled and strongly upturned; sides sloping inwards, posterior corners strongly rounded, posterior margin straight and concave in the middle; the whole strongly shining thorax has a distinct median longitudinal groove. Tibiae without spines. Abdomen with distinct conical three-segmented appendages; the anal appendages of both sexes are small, separate points.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: One dried worker obtained by Burmeister together with the alates is 7 mm long and appears fully grown. Uniformly pale yellow, the head slightly darker, ochraceous yellow, the compound eyes and the anterior corners of the frons blackish, the ocelli faintly indicated by two red dots. Head large and round, strongly shining, as in the alate, with a transverse impression on the frons. Antennae 27-segmented, slightly longer than the head, otherwise as in the alate. Pronotum half as wide as the head, divided into two equal halves by the transverse groove, with a deeper impression on each side of the groove; anterior margin semicircular, upturned; posterior margin semicircular; the narrow anterior corners projecting forwards are rounded and strongly bent down. Mesothorax and metathorax wider, the sides sloping, distinctly widening posteriorly, posterior margin strongly rounded. Body oval, abdominal appendages very small, anal appendages two, long, stout and separate from each other. Legs slender and long, extending beyond the body. Hairs fairly dense. Thirteen other dried specimens agree with it, 4—7 mm long, collected by Schaum at Cairo and by Ehrenberg in Egypt; several of them have smaller heads and, judging by their very small triangular wing pads, are larvae.
